summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Greifswald, Bonn, Berlin, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, and Lassen. He became Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Breslau (1833) and sub-librarian at Wrocław University Library (1834–1872).

Adolf Holtzmann the Elder was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. From 1852 to 1870, he served as Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University.
Adolf Kaegi was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Rudolf von Roth from circa 1873 to 1875. He held a professorship at the University of Zurich from circa 1883 to 1923.

Adolf Kirchhoff worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1842–1846) and later held positions at Humboldt University and Frederick William University Berlin from circa 1865 to 1908.

Adolphe Régnier was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held a professorship in Latin eloquence at the Collège de France (~1862–1884) and held a post at the Palace of Fontainebleau (~1873–1884).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He has held posts at Columbia International University Korntal and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and held a post at the University of Warsaw attested in 2008.

Agathon Benary was a linguistics scholar who studied at Göttingen, Berlin under Franz Bopp, and Halle-Wittenberg. From circa 1833 to 1860, he held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and as a professor at Köllnisches Gymnasium.

Agehananda Bharati was an Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna. He held positions at Delhi, Banaras Hindu, Tokyo, Kyoto, and Washington universities, and was professor of anthropology at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw, and completed a PhD at Nicolaus Copernicus University. She held affiliations with Cornell University (~2008–2010) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Ahmad Hasan Dani was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington at Banaras Hindu University and London. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar (Department of Archaeology head, ~1962–1971), and Quaid-i-Azam (Arts Dean, 1988).

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Bedford College and under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He was co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) and became Abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery circa 2010.
Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Emmanuel College, University of Cambridge (~1969–1972) and under Boonman Poonyathiro (~1970–1974).

Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a pupil under Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya. He held a post as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Akifumi Naito specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji-ha Shogakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao. He held posts at the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism, Ryukoku University, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Paris. His academic appointments include posts at Kyoto University (~1983–1986; Professor ~2003–2018) and Kyushu University (~1986–2003).
Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University. He later held posts there, attested as a lecturer in 1992 and as Professor of Buddhist Studies in 2013.

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her studies at Aoyama Gakuin University and Harvard University, and held a post at the University of Oregon from 2009 to 2016.

Akimichi Eda is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang, and earned a Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg under doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn (attested 2005).

Akio Donohashi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1968 to 1977 and served as a professor at Kobe University from circa 1990 to 2012.
